newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks comment on oil drilling in Alaskan area.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks comment on oil drilling in Alaskan area.

text.p: The Interior Department said it would issue a notice Thursday seeking comments from the public on how to protect wildlife and the land while allowing oil and gas leasing in Alaska's National Petroleum Reserve (NPR-A).
The department plans to decide by August 15, 1998 whether to open a 4.6 million acre portion of the reserve to oil and gas leasing.
Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt added that he would visit the reserve this summer to "spend some time familiarizing myself with the issues within the planning area."
The NPR-A lies between the Brooks Range on the East and the Arctic Ocean on the West.
Three oil companies last October announced a major oil find on the western border of the reserve, renewing interest in the area.
The NPR-A is far west of the coastal plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, another area which oil companies want to open to drilling which the Clinton administration opposes.
